{{nihongo|'''Shioyuhiko Shrine'''|塩湯彦神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Dewa Province]].

'''Shioyuhiko Shrine''' (しおゆひこじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Yokote, Akita|Q496479|qid=Q496479}}, {{ill|Akita Prefecture|Q81863|qid=Q81863}}<ref name="akita">Hisae Otomo, "Shioyuhiko Shrine," 'Akita Daihyakka Jiten,' Akita Sakigake Shinpo, 1981, ISBN 4870200074</ref>. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|ja|式内小社|simple|Shikinai Shosha|qid=Q134917287}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} and was formerly ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

=== Origin ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=En no Gyōja}} in {{ill|672|Q30601|qid=Q30601}} ({{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 12). It appears in the '{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}' as "Shioyuhiko Shrine, Hiraka District, Dewa Province," i.e., a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}<ref name=akita/><ref name=jinjacho>[https://akita-jinjacho.sakura.ne.jp/tatsujin_etc/01_jinja/yokote/043_sioyuhiko.html "Shioyuhiko Shrine" official site of Akita Prefecture Shrine Office]</ref>. It seems originally to have been a hot-spring deity of Mount Ontake rising east of the Hiraka basin<ref name=akita/>, but under influence of {{ill|Kumano Three Shrines|Q10403700|qid=Q10403700|lt=Kumano}}-line {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}}<ref name=akita/> it came to be called "Kumano-dō" in the medieval period. Likely for that reason, Hayatama-no-Mikoto is enshrined.

After a period of decline<ref name=akita/>, the Otomo family, priests of {{ill|Horowasan Haushiwake Shrine|Q11385699|qid=Q11385699}} (another Shikinaisha in the same district), served as {{ill|Bettō|Q2900274|qid=Q2900274}}, while the Minashi family in charge of kagura managed it in practice. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, when {{ill|Satake Yoshitada|Q8514533|qid=Q8514533}}, lord of {{ill|Kubota Domain|Q1067720|qid=Q1067720|lt=Akita Domain}}, restored old shrines within the domain, this shrine was also restored, and it was revered through the Edo period as one of Akita Domain's Three Province Shrines. In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5), it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

In {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 38), heavy snow caused the shrine buildings to collapse, and ritual functions shifted to the satomiya; in {{ill|1982|Q2436|qid=Q2436}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 57), it was rebuilt by local supporters<ref name=jinjacho/><ref>[http://www.city.yokote.lg.jp/kanko/page000059.html "Shioyuhiko Shrine (Sannai)" official site of {{ill|Yokote, Akita|Q496479|qid=Q496479}}]</ref>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
{{ill|Kumano Gongen|Q11568925|qid=Q11568925|lt=Hayatama-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}<ref name=akita/><ref name=jinjacho/>

=== Festivals ===
* {{ill|July 21|Q2727|qid=Q2727}}: annual festival<ref name=jinjacho/>

=== Outside/associated shrines ===
* '''Satomiya''': '''Shioyuhiko Tsurugaike Shrine''' (Tsurugaike, Tsuchibuchi, Sannai, Yokote)
* '''Inner sanctuary''': '''Shirataki Kannon''' (Kannonzawa, Oomatsukawa, Sannai, Yokote)

=== Scenic / historic points ===
* The foothills of Mount Ontake where this shrine stands are the northern limit of large clusters of {{ill|Camellia rusticana|Q11345564|qid=Q11345564}}.
* Around the satomiya, Tsurugaike Park is developed, and hot springs are nearby.

=== Other ===
Possibly due to faith around Shirataki Kannon, treated as this shrine's inner sanctuary, it is unusual for a {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}} mountain in that women were not prohibited from old times.
